newsitem.title: THAILAND: British drug woman leaves Thailand for UK jail.
newsitem.headline: British drug woman leaves Thailand for UK jail.

text.p: Convicted British drugs trafficker Sandra Gregory left Thailand for home late on Wednesday night to serve the remainder of her sentence in a prison in Britain, a Thai immigration official said.
Amid tight security, she was escorted by a group of Thai and British officials in a motorcade to the tarmac at Bangkok international airport and put on a British Airways flight to London.
She was accompanied on the flight by three other British prisoners, also convicted and jailed by Thai courts for drug offences, the official told Reuters.

Earlier in the day, a group of British officials who arrived in Thailand to handle the case, arranged with Thai prison authorities for Gregory and the three other convicts to be released from prisons here so they could complete their terms in Britain.
Thai authorities took extra measures to keep Gregory away from a band of local and foreign journalists who tried to speak to her ahead of her departure.

When she was brought to the immigration department in a van in the late afternoon, Gregory dressed in white, was bundled into the office through a side entrance by her escorts to complete travel procedures.
As reporters shouted questions to her, she replied: "Feel good. Feel Good."

Gregory, from Halifax in northern England, was detained with Robert Lock from Cambridge in February 11993, as they were about to board a flight to Japan. Anti-narcotics police found 102 grams (3.6 ounces) of heroin in her possession.
She pleaded guilty but told the court that Lock had paid her to smuggle the heroin out of Thailand.
In February 1996, she was sentenced to 25 years in jail for heroin smuggling. A death sentence was commuted because she confessed and Lock was found not guilty.
The departure of the four convicts to serve out their jail terms in Britain was made possible under a bilateral pact between Thailand and Britain.
Under the pact signed in 1991, Britons who have served a certain amount of time in Thailand can apply to be sent home to serve the remainder of their sentence.
Gregory has served four years and four months of her term.
Thirty-three British citizens, mostly convicted of drugs offences, are serving jail terms in Thailand, an interior ministry source said.
